mechanism: The closed --analyze-retained-discovery descriptor receives the existing native analysis Request plus supplied discovered_sources. It compares the complete supplied inventory of native nondeclaration roots against captured text before invoking actual analyze. Successful output retains the actual native analysis; mismatch output has SOURCE_SNAPSHOT_MISMATCH and no native_analysis.
authority: Accepted ADR0037 and frozen public P01/N01 capture-versus-discovered-content contract. Current analyze.ts assertSnapshotInputs and plane-a-runtime.ts distinguish capture consistency from runtime composition. This checkpoint exercises distinct DEV inputs, not those frozen consumers.
scope: At least one native nondeclaration TS/JS source root; String text capture only. Canonical root/capture keys use the existing measured-case normalizer; discovery coordinates must be canonical portable relative paths. Declaration annex roots do not belong to the supplied source inventory. No autodiscovery, role/language remapping, whole retained scope, capture atomicity or complete public Plane-A runtime claim.
failurePaths: Missing/null/malformed/foreign descriptor fields refuse with a named invalid-request observation.
Missing/foreign/duplicate discovered sources, conflicting root/capture aliases, invalid relative paths, empty/declaration-only roots and unsupported source extensions refuse.
Retained=false or raw/UTF16 captures refuse in this new bounded operation; existing raw/UTF16 analysis paths remain unchanged.
Missing captured text or any changed discovered text, including CRLF/BOM, yields SOURCE_SNAPSHOT_MISMATCH before native analysis. Physical live content is not substituted.
Wrong CLI argument count, unreadable descriptor/SDK and malformed transport JSON fail nonzero through the existing main router; these are not structured semantic refusals.
identities: Original Request/raw/batch/worker schemas are unchanged. Separate private descriptor, supplied SDK and executable identities bind both successful and semantic-refusal observations; successful inner native analysis retains its actual Request and input bindings.
